docs_page.cli_intro: Install any community skill locally with a single `skills` command.
docs_page.cli_prereq_p1: Install Node.js from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org) (it ships with `npm`), then verify:
docs_page.cli_login_p1: First generate a token at [{site}/settings/tokens]({site}/settings/tokens) (it is shown only once — copy it right away), then:
docs_page.cli_login_p2: After logging in, every command targets this site by default — no need to pass `--registry` again.
docs_page.cli_install_p1: Every skill's detail page has an "Install" box pre-filled with `skills install '<slug>'` — just copy and run. Restricted skills must be requested first: click "Request download" on the detail page and wait for the author's approval before installing.
docs_page.cli_install_p2: Packs are admin-curated skill bundles organized by scenario (see the "Packs" tab on the browse page); a single `pack:` command installs them all — if one item fails (e.g. restricted and not yet approved), the rest still install.
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p1: When the site ships a new CLI version (e.g. adding `pack:` pack installs), upgrade with one command:
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p2: Note the difference: `skills update` updates **the skills you have installed**; `skills upgrade` upgrades the `skills` **command itself**.
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p3: If your CLI is too old to have the `upgrade` command yet, just reinstall it once manually (it will be available afterwards):
docs_page.cli_uninstall_p1: Uninstalling the CLI does not touch the skill files already installed locally. To remove a skill, just delete its directory: `.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` inside a project, `~/.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` globally.
docs_page.authoring_intro: Every skill is essentially a `SKILL.md` file — a block of YAML frontmatter at the top, followed by a Markdown body written for Claude.
docs_page.authoring_frontmatter_table:
| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | ✓ | Skill name, shown on the card |
| `description` | ✓ | One-line description, 140 characters max |
| `version` | ✓ | Follows semver, e.g. 1.2.0 |
| `license` |  | Defaults to MIT |
| `triggers` |  | Keywords that make Claude auto-activate this skill |
| `dependencies` |  | Slugs of other skills it depends on, comma-separated |
docs_page.authoring_h_tips: 3. Tips for writing a good body
docs_page.authoring_tip_1: **Say how to do it, directly.** A skill is written for Claude, not marketing copy for humans. State its core capability in the very first paragraph.
docs_page.authoring_tip_2: **List trigger conditions separately** so Claude can tell at a glance when to use the skill.
docs_page.authoring_tip_3: **Do not write a prompt prefix** (like "You are playing the role of…"). Claude is already acting as an agent and does not need to be "commanded" — write the rules and workflow directly.
docs_page.authoring_tip_4: **Put examples last.** If you have input/output examples, place them at the end of the skill under a `## Examples` heading.
docs_page.authoring_length_table:
| Token range | Suited for |
|---|---|
| < 800 | Micro utilities — simple prompt rewrites, format checks |
| 800-2K | Standard skills — most use cases |
| 2K-5K | Complex skills — multi-step workflows + multiple trigger scenarios |
| > 5K | Not recommended — split into several skills that cooperate via composition |
docs_page.authoring_length_note: The platform shows the token cost you declare (entered manually at creation) on the skill card, so users can pick accordingly.
docs_page.authoring_upload_form: **Form mode**: fill in the form on the site and write the Markdown body directly — good for simple skills
docs_page.authoring_upload_pack: **Package mode**: upload a zip (containing SKILL.md plus optional script files) — good for skills that ship helper scripts
docs_page.authoring_upload_note: Either way, you can edit and publish new versions after uploading (semver, strictly increasing); subscribers get an update notice.
docs_page.authoring_remix_1: **Credit the source** in your forked skill — e.g. "based on `xxxxx`"
docs_page.authoring_remix_2: If the original license has requirements, keep it (permissive licenses like MIT impose none)
docs_page.authoring_remix_3: For major changes, rename the skill and position it as its own thing instead of confusing people with a near-identical name
docs_page.authoring_sample_description: Detects PDF form fields, fills them in and places the signature.
docs_page.authoring_sample_what_body: (One or two paragraphs stating exactly what this Skill is for)
docs_page.authoring_sample_trigger_1: The request mentions "sign pdf", "fill out form" or similar
